question: Where should the reusable part live?

options.label: Split (Recommended)
options.description: Process, checklist, render tool and reviewer go in a reusable skill (e.g. in osaskills); the brief, references, theme, components and taste log stay in this repo.

options.label: This project only
options.description: Everything lives in the repo (e.g. .claude/roblox/ui.md). Simpler, but it can't be reused in other games without copying.

options.label: Reusable skill only
options.description: One skill holds it all, including a default look. Each game would start from the same taste.

question: Where should the visual direction come from?

options.label: Your references (Recommended)
options.description: You drop screenshots of games/UIs you like (and dislike) into docs/design/refs; I turn them into a brief you approve.

options.label: I research, you pick
options.description: I gather UI from popular Roblox games in your genre and show you 3-4 directions to choose from.

options.label: Adjectives first
options.description: You describe the feel in words (genre, mood, 'not like X'); I propose a direction from that.

question: How should design ideas be explored?

options.label: Studio only (Recommended)
options.description: Every version is a real Vide story rendered in Studio, so what you approve is what ships. Slower per round.

options.label: HTML first, then port
options.description: Fast mockups in the browser, then rebuilt in Vide. Quicker to explore, but some designs won't carry over to Roblox.

pick: I'm going to give you some stuff to research and examine.

question: How often do you want to weigh in on a screen?

options.label: Direction + final (Recommended)
options.description: You pick from the versions and review the finished screen; the reviewer and I handle the rounds in between.

options.label: Every round
options.description: You see each rendered sheet before I change anything. Most control, most of your time.

options.label: Final only
options.description: I pick the direction myself from the brief and taste log; you review the result.

question: When do you want to pick a direction?

options.label: Tiles once + major screens (Recommended)
options.description: 3 style tiles at the start set the game's look; after that, 2–3 layout options for major screens only (shop, inventory, HUD). Minor screens go straight to your final review.

options.label: Style tiles once only
options.description: Pick the look once; every screen after that comes to you finished.

options.label: 3 directions per screen
options.description: Every screen gets 3 full options. The most control, but the slowest and costliest.

question: Which model should the reviewer subagent run on?

options.label: Opus (Recommended)
options.description: Best eye for subtle visual problems. Up to 3 reviews per screen, so cost scales with screen count.

options.label: Sonnet
options.description: Cheaper per review; more likely to miss spacing, weight and hierarchy issues.

question: How should the skill handle rhr's four bugs (wrapper project, string requires, Vide's profiler calls, the font override)?

options.label: Pinned launcher (Recommended)
options.description: The fixes live in a small launcher script in the skill that only runs on rhr 1.0.0rc1. File the bugs upstream later and delete each fix as it lands.

options.label: Fork rhr
options.description: Keep our own fork with the fixes and install from it. Sturdier, but we take on merging upstream changes.

question: Should check.sh stop UI code from using raw style values instead of the theme?

options.label: Fail on raw values (Recommended)
options.description: check.sh fails on literal colors, fonts and text sizes in UI components and screens; they must come from Theme.luau. Keeps every screen on the same scale.

options.label: Reviewer flags them
options.description: No check.sh rule; the reviewer calls out values that aren't from the theme.

options.label: No guard
options.description: Rely on the stories and your review.

question: Roblox's docs say a background is stretched to the full screen only if it covers the whole device safe area, top-bar strip included. App's full-size frames sit below the 58 px top bar, so on a phone in Play they wouldn't fill the notch strips. Studio's Edit emulator has no top bar, which is why it filled them in our capture. Which rule should rhr follow?

options.label: Roblox's documented rule (Recommended)
options.description: Stretch a background only when it covers the device safe area. On phone renders, App's full-size frames stay inside the notch insets. A backdrop using DeviceSafeInsets or IgnoreGuiInset fills the strips. The Edit capture matches too, because it has no top bar.

options.label: Fill if it fills its ScreenGui
options.description: Treat the ScreenGui's own area as the safe area, so App's full-size backgrounds also fill the notch and top-bar strips. That matches the Edit capture, but the docs say Play doesn't do it.

options.label: Check in Play first
options.description: I run a solo Play probe on the iPhone 16 emulator with a full-size coloured frame, and you tell me whether the notch strips next to it are coloured. It takes a few minutes of your time.

question: How should rhr draw scroll bars that set custom TopImage, MidImage or BottomImage?

options.label: Default pill for all (Recommended)
options.description: Every bar is drawn as Roblox's default pill in its ScrollBarImageColor3 and transparency. Custom images are listed as an approximation in rhr's docs. Your game has no custom bar images yet.

options.label: Draw custom images
options.description: Draw the three images (top cap, stretched middle, bottom cap) when they're in the asset cache, and fall back to the pill offline. This means more work: slicing, plus guessing how the horizontal bar rotates them.

pick: this is supposed to be a reusable, reliable workflow

question: Push the six commits to your fork and reinstall rhr from it?

options.label: Push and reinstall (Recommended)
options.description: git push origin main: a fast-forward of osabased/roblox-headless-renderer, with nothing sent upstream. Then reinstall with uv tool install from GitHub at 8b3b0b6, the same way osabased.1 was installed, and confirm rhr --version prints 1.0.0rc1+osabased.2.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Keep the commits local. The installed rhr stays at osabased.1, without these fixes.

question: Remove the rhr-fidelity feedback loop once osabased.2 is installed?

options.label: Remove after install (Recommended)
options.description: The fork's own tests already cover the same Studio cases. Notes that still apply move into the rhr-fork memory. Then loops/rhr-fidelity (check.py, the Studio probe scripts, the measurement notes) and its memory entry are deleted.

options.label: Keep for now
options.description: Keep it as a Studio-checked reference until the follow-up fixes (in-world scroll bars, Global z-order) are done.

question: Save this correction to the play-test section of .claude/roblox/checks.md?

options.label: Save it (Recommended)
options.description: Replace the one wrong sentence about screen_capture, as shown in the preview. Then run check.sh, leave the change uncommitted, and drop the matching clause from the memory that notes the conflict.
options.preview:
Before:
`screen_capture` only works in edit mode, so it can't show play-test UI.

After:
`screen_capture` also works in a play-test, the device emulator included, but its JPG is smaller than the screen (627x288 for an 874x401 screen), so scale its coordinates up to the screen's.

options.label: Leave it
options.description: Keep the guide as it is. The memory that notes the conflict stays.

question: Should `rhr check` report an image that rhr can't draw as an `image-missing` finding, or only list it in the render reports' missingAssets?

options.label: Report it, as info (Recommended)
options.description: `image-missing` covers every image rhr can't draw, with the reason. An id Roblox refused stays a warning, because Roblox won't show it either. rbxasset://, rbxthumb:// and other gaps only rhr has become info: Roblox draws those, so a build gate set to warnings won't fail on them. An id that just isn't downloaded yet isn't reported, since `rhr check` never downloads and `rhr ui` would fetch it.

options.label: Report it, as a warning
options.description: Same list, but every entry is a warning. A gate at --min-severity warning then fails on UIs that look right in Roblox.

options.label: Only list it in missingAssets
options.description: `rhr check` keeps reporting only ids Roblox refused. The render reports (`ui`, `scene`, `preview` --json) list everything else.

question: rhr could draw rbxasset:// UI images from the local Studio install's content folder, the way its 3D renderer already draws rbxasset:// decals. It won't be built here. Should I propose it as its own session?

options.label: Yes, propose it (Recommended)
options.description: I'll leave a New task card for a separate session. Until that lands, these images stay blank and listed.

options.label: No, keep them listed only
options.description: rbxasset:// UI images stay blank. missingAssets names them with the reason.

question: The sunburst remap in postprocess.py has no recorded reason: it arrived in upstream's first public commit (22c9aca) with no test or doc, and "Custom/Sunburst" isn't defined anywhere else in the repo. What should I do with it?

options.label: Remove it (Recommended)
options.description: An ImageLabel always draws its own Image, or is left undrawn and listed in missingAssets when RHR can't draw it. Adds tests for "GrayscaleIcon" (cached image drawn) and "Rays" (missing image listed, nothing drawn), plus changelog and version bump (next +osabased.11).

options.label: Keep, but narrow it
options.description: Remap only when the Image is empty and the name is exactly Sunburst/SunRays. Still draws a picture Roblox doesn't.

options.label: Leave as is
options.description: Make no change; I'd just report the findings.
